main_text.p: pede vinciebantur, quam ποδυνηγικλω[?] dicebant. Ea lignum erat, in quod pedes captivorum inserebantur, ac vincti tenebantur in carcere, quinque, septem, decem dies, prout judices aequum & justum esse pro vincti conditione & criminis modo statuebant, ut ex Demosthene & Lysiâ cognoscimus.

AD rem militarem pertinebant leges hae: Si quis clypeum abjecerit aut amiserit in bello, drachmarum D multâ culpam luito. Lysias in Theomnestea. Quem ordinem quisque in militiâ sibi assignatum acceperit, eum teneto, nec pro arbitrio suo mutato: gravis armaturâ milesin equites se non transferto, & contrà: qui ex gravi armaturâ ad ordinem equestrem injussu conceßerit, infamiâ notator: non solum qui ex pugnâ fugiens ordinem deseruerit, sed etiam, qui cum miles scriptus in militia praesens esse debuerat, abesset. Idem Lysias in oratione contra Alcibiadem.
Emoratu[?] digna est lex funebris, quam posteritatis memoriae con-vavit Demosthenes contra Macarta-n[?], latam olim à Solone: Defunctum, ait

page.notes: The Greek word on the first line ("ποδυνηγικλω") is doubtful; the printed letters are not fully legible. The drachma sign "D" before "multâ" is doubtful. "milesin" is a printing error for "miles in" and is left as printed. The initial word of the last paragraph and the Macartatum word are doubtful: the large initial letter overlaps and the line is partly faded. "con-vavit" is unclear. A small mark stands after "Alcibiadem." and is not transcribed. The left-edge marks are show-through from the facing page and are not transcribed.
